title.narrative: Greater Mekong Subregion Biodiversity Conservation Corridors Project (Cambodia, Lao People's Democratic Republic, and Viet Nam)

description.narrative: The Project will enhance transboundary cooperation for preventing and mitigating fragmentation of biodiversity rich forest landscapes of the Cardamom Mountains and Eastern Plains Dry Forest in Cambodia, Triborder Forest areas located in southern Lao PDR, and the Central Annamites in Viet Nam.

title.narrative: Reports and Recommendations of the President

description.narrative: Output/s as listed by the project staff.

Output: Biodiversity conservation landscape managed with ecosystem services protected and maintained Indicator: About 19,500 ha of natural forest land rehabilitated through forest restoration, enrichment planting, non-timber forest product and agroforestry planting using mainly native species Progress/Status: CAM: i. Three mangrove nurseries and five upland nurseries were established in both targeted provinces including one nursery at the Forest Research Station in KKG (100% of target).
ii. An area of 3,154.7 ha of natural forest land were rehabilitated (124% of target).
iii. An area of 602 ha of agroforestry was established (100% of target) with 571 beneficiaries (163% of target).
iv. Labor for restoration activities included 36,691/F16,933 (46.2% women - 115% of target). (CPAs were 19,304/F8,797 (45.6% women) and CFs were 17,387/F8,136 (46.8% women).
LAO: - The areas planted were completed in 2016 as per the Forestry Plan. Over 2017-2018, 3,542 ha of ANR established with 594.53 ha in CPS, 809 ha in SK and 769 ha in ATP. - 1,450 ha of tree planted in CPS 280 ha, SK 437 ha and ATP 733 ha. - NTFP planting plots: CPS 48 ha, ATP 5 ha and SK 5 ha. - Women's labor input was 86,083 ps-days (50.3%) out of the total 186,385 ps-days of labor for forest restoration. - 138 signs were completely erected at ANR sites in Pathoumphone. Whilst the signs installation in other 2 provinces is still going on. -Survival rates survey undertaken on the total area of 216.06 ha of plantation from 2014, 2015 and 2016 in 13 villages of PTP, CPS with an average survival rate of 74.49%.
VIE: Community forest management plan prepared for 13,685 ha. Government is to finance its implementation after project completion. Data Source: Performance monitoring survey/reports; CPCU reports Actual value:

Output: Biodiversity conservation landscape managed with ecosystem services protected and maintained Indicator: At least 392,000 ha of biodiversity corridors patrolled and protected Progress/Status: CAM: Patrolling activities were achieved in 2014 in 23 communities covering an area of 47,937 ha (100% of target).
LAO: - Village patrol teams were formed, equipped and operational in all 36 BCC priority villages (SK 14, ATP 7, CPS 15) identified by the biodiversity assessment. - Patrolling plans were developed to ensure effectiveness in dealing with the environmental crime in the corridors. - So far 352,940 ha conservation and protection forests areas have been patrolled. - 397 cases recorded of which are 254 cases of illegal logging, 74 cases of hunting, 67 cases of encroachment on land and 2 illegal NTFP gathering respectively. Against these events, 129 actions taken with 89 education/oral warning and 40 of written notice.
VIE: Patrolling commenced since 2013 but not consistent due to scope change during MTR in 2014 and insufficient fund allocation. Data Source: Reports of forest procetion department on illegal activities Actual value:

Output: Institutions and communities strengthened in biodiversity corridor management Indicator: Collective forestland (management certificates provided to 22 commune in CAM & 69 villages in Lao PDR; in VIE 13,700 ha receive new land use certificates, of which 1,500 ha are for individual households with certification to at least 50%of households headed by women. Progress/Status: CAM: Boundaries were demarcated for nine CPAs and 14 CFs (100% of target).
LAO: PLUPs are completed for all 67 villages and approved by the provincial authority.
VIE: Partly achieved with with 03 year delay. LUC issued for 4,625 ha production forest vs 6,000ha of DMF target. Underachievement is due to (i) maximum forest areas identified for plantation in TTH, (ii) low interest of local residents to participate in the project in Quang Tri due to long delay of the activities. Data Source: Land use certificates Actual value:

Output: Institutions and communities strengthened in biodiversity corridor management Indicator: Demarcation of 880 km completed in the corridors in three countries Progress/Status: CAM: CPA management guidelines were approved by MOE in January 2017 (100% of target).
LAO: Demarcation of the corridor boundaries in Sekong (136km), Attapeu (164km) and Champasak (118km) have been completed
VIE: Achieved with 03 year delay. Revised total number of villages is now 37 instead of 40. All 37 CFM boards established (13 villages in TTH, 14 villages in QN, 10 villages in QT). The remaining 5 expected within Q2/2018. By 2020, LUC issued for 13,685 ha of natural forests (vs target of 10,000ha). Data Source: Demarcation maps Actual value:

Output: Institutions and communities strengthened in biodiversity corridor management Indicator: G0433-VIE: By 2016, one new protected area covering 17,000 ha of land legally established Progress/Status: VIE: Achieved with delay. The decision on establishing Nam Tra My protection forest area (formerly Ngoc Linh PA) in Quang Nam, covering 114,883 ha issued in June 2020. Data Source: Reports of Forest department on protection and illegal activities Actual value:

Output: Institutions and communities strengthened in biodiversity corridor management Indicator: G0433-VIE: By 2016, two new PAMBs established biodiversity protection, conservation and use Progress/Status: Partly achieved with delay. - Ngoc Linh PAMB was established in 2018. - HCM Legendary Trail PA was removed from grant scope, thus its PAMB was not established. This partial achievement does not impact the achievement of grant outcome. Data Source: Project reports Actual value:

Output: Institutions and communities strengthened in biodiversity corridor management Indicator: G0433-VIE: By 2017, members of all eight PAMBs trained on gender issues in sustainable biodiversity protection, conservation and use Progress/Status: Achieved - Training workshops on gender issues in biodiversity protection, conservation, and use were delivered to PAMBs staff during 2017-8. Data Source: Project reports Actual value:

Output: Institutions and communities strengthened in biodiversity corridor management Indicator: Participatory landuse plans (PLUP) and commune village investment profiles and plans updated in 22 communes in CAM, 34 communes in VIE and 69 villages in LAO Progress/Status: CAM: The NPASMP that was completed in 2017 by MOE provides the regulatory framework for the maintenance of eco-system services within all PAs including the identified biodiversity corridors (100% of target).
LAO: Participatory land use maps were completed for 67 villages and approved by provincial governors. 126 plots of conservation and protection forests with a total area of 1,261,429 ha in 3 provinces mapped. 71 big sign boards of land use plan and 310 concrete poles were installed along the corridor boundaries.
VIE: Achieved. PLUPs completed in 2015 and final results approved in 2016. CIPs prepared for 35 communes in 2015 and final CIPs approved in 2016 and 2017. Data Source: LUPs with maps for communes; commune profiles & investment plans Actual value:

Output: Institutions and communities strengthened in biodiversity corridor management Indicator: Training at central & local areas with at least 40% female representation: 3,460 in CAM; 2,470 in LAO; & 4,350 in VIE Progress/Status: CAM: Approval of all nine CPAs was achieved by September 2018 (100% of target). Women comprised 46% of the CPA and CF members (153% of target).
Total cumulative number of 882 persons at central level, 1,528 persons at provincial level, 232 persons at district level and 44,154 persons at commune level trained in project activities (3,518% of target). Trainees included 50.9 percent women (127.3% of target).
IPs comprised 88.9% of participants in commune level trainings. (178% of target).
LAO: 1,522 government staff members were trained, of the total number of participants, 45.7% were women. 21,721 villagers including 11,064 women (50.94%) and 3,159 government officials and project's staff including 906 female staff (28.68%) participated in technical, management and safeguards meetings.
VIE: Achieved. (11,211 trainees) with 42% of trainees are female, 85% from ethnic minorities. Data Source: CPCU and NPMO reports Actual value:

Output: Institutions and communities strengthened in biodiversity corridor management Indicator: Zoning of biodiversity corridor: 700,000 ha in CAM, 698,000 ha in LAO & 530,000 ha in VIE Progress/Status: CAM: A total of 1,427,940 hectares of biodiversity corridors with zoning has been completed (204% of target) in the whole country and was approved by RGC on 26 January 2017 of which 927,130 ha is located within the project target provinces (757,661 ha in north-east of the country and 169,469 ha in the Cardamom mountain area).
LAO: A total of 126 plots covering 1,261,429ha conservation and protection forests were issued forest land use certificates, of which 27 plots conservation forest covering 141,624 ha and 9 plots of protection forests covering 100,490 ha in Attapeu; 12 plots of conservation forsts with 60,714 ha and 19 plots of protection forest with 61,621 ha in Sekong; and 23 plots of conservation forests with 84,884 ha and 26 plots of protection forests with 162 ha in Champasak.
VIE: Achieved with three year delay vs target year of 2015. Mapping substantially completed for 521,878 ha. Data Source: Corridor maps approved by provincial governments, MAFF, MOE & MONRE Actual value:

Output: Livelihoods improved, small-scale infrastructure support provided and financial sustainability obtained in target villages with reduced greenhouse gas emissions Indicator: 56 communes in CAM & VIE & 69 villages in LAO receive seed capital valued at $1.45 million for commune and village development (revolving) funds Progress/Status: CAM: Based upon data from LISDI 60% of FHHs in target villages participated in the livelihood activities (60% of target).
LAO: - 67 BCC villages with Village Development Funds (VDF) established. Funds ($5,000 per villages) disbursed to all 67 villages, regulations establish and training provided. -VDF cumulative amount reaches $387,835 (+13.55%). - VDF has been transferred to Lao Women's Union for continued supervision and monitoring since June 2017.
VIE: Achieved. 1,560 hhs were accessed to the loan. Most of people received loan from CDFs are women and ethnic minorities (QT: women are 100%, ethnic minorities are 93%; TTH: women are 69% and ethnic minorities are 85%). However, per MOF instruction, CDF funds had returned to the government budget after the project completion in Sep 2019. Data Source: Provincial business and enterprise statistics
Actual value:

Output: Livelihoods improved, small-scale infrastructure support provided and financial sustainability obtained in target villages with reduced greenhouse gas emissions Indicator: About $18.7 million is disbursed for income-enhancing small-scale infrastructure with capacity building in operation and maintenance and business models (ecotoursim, NTFP, and agroprocessing) Progress/Status: CAM: 14 subprojects were implemented that supported alternative livelihoods featuring different value chains (chicken, honey, bamboo, crab & mussel, melaleuca silviculture, ecotourism, NTFP and agro-processing).
Overall project (Additional Financing (G0426)): i. Construction of 1 lined RHP in Mondulkiri (MDK), seven unlined RHPs (4 in MDK and 3 in Koh Kong (KKG)), 15 borehole wells and five stream water extraction subprojects (all equipped with solar powered pumps and water storage tanks) and 2 community rainwater tank subprojects was completed (representing 78% of the target of 40 subprojects) and 1,435 households benefitted from home gardens and drought resilient crops (72% of target); climate resilient irrigation system in MDK was completed with 90 households benefitting from the dry season irrigation and 402 households adopted SRI techniques (40% of target) including adoption by all households in both target provinces. Two sea barriers were constructed in KKG with a total length of 10.8 km (72% of target) and 351 households benefitted from the adoption of salt tolerant crops (88% of target); 216 households benefitted from diversified income from sustainably managed forest in one catchment area in MDK.
ii. Small scale infrastructure support and livelihood support (LISDI) was provided in all target villages in 22 communes for boreholes/hand pump wells, latrines, household and community office solar, community water tanks and household water filters (of target).
iii. 5 case studies/policy briefs on ecosystem-based adaptation and integration of climate change in design of sea barriers, irrigation, and rainwater harvesting ponds, VDF and home gardens were prepared by IIRR/CEDAC (100% of target).
iv. Training of officials and project staff to acquire capacity to integrate climate change concerns into development planning and budgeting was not completed.
LAO: - out of 65 small scale rural infrastructure subprojects constructed, 32 are fully complete with 100% payment, 28 requires fixing of defects and 4 are under construction and 1 requires additional works.
VIE: Achieved. All 77 SSI subprojects completed and handed over for use in 3 provinces. Data Source: Provincial business and enterprise statistics
Actual value:

Output: Livelihoods improved, small-scale infrastructure support provided and financial sustainability obtained in target villages with reduced greenhouse gas emissions Indicator: At least 30% of CDF management committees are women; at least 30% of CDF investments targeted at livelihood activities prepared and submitted by community women Progress/Status: CAM: 37 VDFSGs were established with supporting management committees (106% of target).
1,219 loans were provided to VDF members and 70% of these have been taken by women (140% of target).
LAO: - 111 groups have been set up with 4,947 beneficiaries of whom 2,503 are women (51%). - depending on local demand and resource availability, the programme covers various livelihoods options, including poultry, pigs and goat raising, home gardening, NTFP planting, etc... with the main focus on supporting opportunities for income generation rather than produce for home consumption.
VIE: Complied with 42% of female members Data Source: Performance monitoring survey/reports Actual value:

Output: Livelihoods improved, small-scale infrastructure support provided and financial sustainability obtained in target villages with reduced greenhouse gas emissions Indicator: At least 4,775 hh and more than 4,000 individual farmers (at least 30% female) receive cash and technical support to improve agricultural productivity and income from home gardens, and agriculture/animal production; At least 2,200 ha of forest based livelihood plantations Progress/Status: CAM: Through the VDFSGs a total of 1,219 households/rural farmers took loans from the group revolving funds to improve agricultural productivity (135% of target).
Overall project (with Additional Financing (G0426)): 71% of trainees on improving home garden productivity and water conservation were women (88% of target); 66% of trainees on the SRI were women (165% of target); 71% of farmers involved in mangrove planting were women (89% of target); 76% of farmers in demonstration plots for salinity-tolerant crops were women; 43% of management positions in WUGs were women (143% of target) and 33% of management positions in forest conservation groups were women (110%); 41% of unskilled laborers for civil works were women- (137%) (irrigation rehabilitation, dyke construction, rainwater harvesting ponds); none of the water user group members trained in O&M were women.
LAO: -68 VDFs organized and are operational in 67 villages with 1,131 members, of whom 647 are women (57.2%). -VDF board composed 340 members (29% women, 66% indigenous representatives, 24% poor people).
VIE: Fully achieved. As of 31 Oct 2017, 1,056 households (362 hhs in QN, 477 hhs in QT, 217 hhs in TTH) received project support. Data Source: Provincial and district economic survey/reports; Provincial revenue reports
Actual value:

Output: Biodiversity conservation landscape managed with ecosystem services protected and maintained Indicator: Grant 0433-VIE: By 2018, at least 30% participants to the implementation of the CFM plans are women Progress/Status: This indicator is monitored under BCC, CFM is not implemented under GEF. Data Source: CPMU reports Actual value:
